I've addressed both parts of the report.

## Root cause of the retry failure

`Files.Add(ctx, body, contentType)` passes the raw `io.Reader` straight to `Raw.Do` → `http.NewRequestWithContext`. For an `*os.File`, Go's `http` package never populates `GetBody`, so `retryTransport` computes `canReplayBody == false` (`pipedrive/retry.go:86`) and its 429 branch returns `canReplayBody` (false) — uploads fail fast while other (body-less) calls retry.

## Fix

Added `(*FilesService).AddFile(ctx, fileName, content, opts...)` (`pipedrive/v1/files.go:140`), mirroring `CallLogsService.AddRecording`. It builds the multipart body via the existing internal `multipartbody.NewFile` helper, which returns a `*bytes.Reader` — a body `http.NewRequest` recognizes and wraps with a working `GetBody`, making 429/5xx retries safe. Users now pass a file name + reader instead of hand-building multipart; for `os.Open` files the content is buffered and replayed on retry.

## Verification

- `TestFilesService_AddFile` asserts method/path, `multipart/form-data` content type, and the uploaded filename/bytes.
- `TestFilesService_AddFile_RetriesOn429` confirms a 429 on a POST upload is retried and succeeds.
- `go test ./...` passes; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.

Note I left `Add` and `Update` as-is (low-level, still pass-through) since the report only called out `Files.Add`, avoiding a breaking change to the stable API.

Honest caveat: `AddFile` buffers the whole file into memory to make it replayable (same tradeoff as `AddRecording`); very large uploads would use the existing `Add` with a self-managed seekable body instead.
